glosses: To lose one’s traction on a slippery surface; to slide due to a lack of friction.

examples.text: [...] but in the damp conditions prevailing the driver sensibly was unwilling to attempt the climb up through Combe Down tunnel without help, for fear of slipping to a standstill in the unventilated bore, […]

Fernando Amorebieta seemed to have checked him, but a stepover created a fraction of room that became significant as the defender slipped, giving Falcao just enough space to curl a superb finish into the top corner.

glosses: To err.

examples.text: There is one that slippeth in his speach, but not from his heart, and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?

glosses: To accidentally reveal a secret or otherwise say something unintentionally.
To move or fly (out of place); to shoot; often with out, off, etc.

examples.text: A bone may slip out of place.

glosses: To elude or evade by smooth movement.

examples.text: I caught the thief, but he slipped my grasp and ran away.

glosses: To pass (a note, money, etc.), often covertly.

examples.text: She thanked the porter and slipped a ten-dollar bill into his hand.

glosses: To cause to move smoothly and quickly; to slide; to convey gently or secretly.

examples.text: Tvvo other VVitneſſes gave the follovving Evidence; That in his officious Attendance upon his Miſtreſs, he had try'd to ſlip a Povvder into her Drink, and that he vvas once catch'd endeavouring to ſtifle her vvith a Pillovv as ſhe vvas aſleep; […]

“This is a very urgent message for the countess’ ears alone,” replied Rokoff. “Tell her that she must arise and slip something about her and come to the telephone. I shall call up again in five minutes.”

glosses: To move quickly and often secretively; to depart, withdraw, enter, appear, intrude, or escape as if by sliding.

examples.text: Some errors slipped into the appendix.
Thrice the flitting shadow slipped away.
Thus one tradesman slips away, / To give his partner fairer play.
We slipped along the hedges, noiseless and swift […]
Keith wants to have it both ways. He has engaged me in a political debate, but when his politics are challenged he slips behind a smoke-screen of anti-intellectualism.
He was grey and had eight legs, and could travel anywhere and slip into any corner of 9 worlds. For this reason he was called Sleipnir ("the slipper) and was given to Oðinn as his steed.

glosses: To move down; to slide.

examples.text: Profits have slipped over the past six months.

The Cottagers had previously gone eight games without a win and had slipped into the relegation zone over Christmas, with boss Hughes criticised by fans after their 3-1 home defeat by fellow basement battlers West Ham on Boxing Day.

glosses: To release (a dog, a bird of prey, etc.) to go after a quarry.

examples.text: Lucento slipped me like his greyhound.
'Well, it was one morning early in the spring,' said Lars, 'that I started for Linderudsœter, where I slipped Rap, and he was soon in full cry and made the hillside ring.'

glosses: Clipping of sideslip (“to fly with the longitudinal axis misaligned with the relative wind”).
To remove the skin of a soft fruit, such as a tomato or peach, by blanching briefly in boiling water, then transferring to cold water so that the skin peels, or slips, off easily.
To omit; to lose by negligence.

examples.text: And slip no advantage / That may secure you.

glosses: To cut slips from; to cut; to take off; to make a slip or slips of.

examples.text: to slip a piece of cloth or paper

glosses: To cause to slip or slide off, or out of place.

examples.text: A horse slips his bridle; a dog slips his collar.

glosses: To bring forth (young) prematurely; to slink.
To cause (a schedule or release, etc.) to go, or let it go, beyond the allotted deadline.

examples.text: We have been consistently slipping the product release schedules.

As for trains, the contract was due to be awarded last year, but Rayner confirms that this has slipped and will now be awarded next year.

glosses: An act or instance of slipping.

examples.text: I had a slip on the ice and bruised my hip.

glosses: A woman's undergarment worn under a skirt or dress to conceal unwanted nudity that may otherwise be revealed by the skirt or dress itself; a shift.
A slipdress.
A mistake or error.

examples.text: He took a screamer at slip.

examples.text: We stalked over the extensive plains with Killbuck and Lena in the slips, in search of deer.
